verdicts.evidence: A wrapped-Gaussian counterexample (R~Uniform[-π,π), S_next=(R+wrapped_normal) mod 2π, σ=0.25) satisfies all named assumptions (positivity [0.172,0.828], relevance, completeness, no-future-dependence) yet the partial L2 norms of inverse Fourier coefficients diverge: 3.88, 21.25, 3.99e8, 6.13e21 at cutoffs 5/10/20/30, proving no square-integrable bridge exists under only the stated assumptions.

Source text contains the exact condition S_{t+1}⊥̸R_t|S_t,A_t,O_t=1; an independent simulation of 60,000 observations (52,580 observed) shows residual Pearson r=0.2528 (p=0) and MSE reduction from 0.01706 to 0.01596 when adding next state.

Source extraction confirms Theorem 5.8 contains ||b̂-b*||_2, τ_t δ_t, max{1,||b_t*||²}, and probability 1-3ζ; a finite-dimensional reduction across 2,000 random inverse problems (dims 3–13) yields 0 violations of ||e||≤τ||Te|| with worst ratio 0.871.

Source confirms T², τ_max, √(log(c₁T/ζ)), n^{-α_min/(2α_min+1)}, and log n in the theorem; backward recurrence unrolled for horizons 2–32 matches explicit weighted sums exactly, concentrability products stay below K=3.463, and nonparametric exponents α/(2α+1) remain below 1/2 for α∈{0.6,1,2,4}.

Source contains exact condition O_t⊥(S_{t+1:T},R_{t+1:T})|S_t,A_t,R_t; AST inspection confirms the simulator's missingness logit uses only current state/action/reward; nested logistic fit on 60,000 samples gives LR p=0.1468 and per-sample NLL gain 3.2e-5 when adding future states.

overall: The logbook rigorously falsifies Claim 1 via a mathematically sound infinite-dimensional counterexample showing the named assumptions alone do not guarantee bridge existence (the paper's appendix adds Hilbert-Schmidt and Picard summability conditions). Claims 2–5 are verified through systematic source-text extraction, AST inspection of the official simulator, and statistical diagnostics on 60,000 simulated observations.
